The petitioners being the accused persons in connection with Posta Police Station Case No.175 dated 30th December, 2019 under Sections 405/420/468/471/120B of the Indian Penal Code Ramjiwan Kanoria & Ors vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116982094/
1 corresponding to G.R. No.1513 of 2013 pending before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, 1 st Court at Calcutta has filed the instant revision praying for quashing of the above-mentioned police case.

sentences.text: Indisputably, premises No.22 and 22/1, M.D. Road within the jurisdiction of Posta police station and certain business under the name and style Messers.

T.D.Kumar & Bros. Ltd. comprise of Debottar property on the basis of a deed of trust created by one Nitish Chandra Ghosh on 1st June,
1970.
After his death, trustees were gradually changing on the death of one of the trustees or the other.
In the year 2018, one Mala Ghosh, Smt. Punam Ghosh and Smt. Madhurima Bhattacharya were the trustees.
It is the case of the de-facto complainant that on the death of Smt. Mala Ghosh, he was inducted as a trustee by board resolution dated 17th September, 2019.

It is alleged by the de-facto complainant that accused No.8 and 9 used to act as Manager to look after the trust property and in course of their regular discharging of function, they obtained absolute faith of the trustees.

Subsequently, with the help of other accused persons, premises No.22 and 22/1, M.D.Road was transferred by way of a long term lease on the basis of power of attorney allegedly executed by the erstwhile trustees in favour of the accused No.1 and 2.

It is the case of the de-facto complainant that the said deeds were executed by the power of attorney holder obtaining signature of the trustees who were women and did not have much knowledge about the property rights executed and registered the deed of lease in question by exerting undue influence upon the trustees.
Therefore, the trustees filed Title Suit No.716 of 2020 for declaration that the lease deed executed on 19 th April, 2012 on the basis of the power of attorney bad in law, illegal and in operative.
It is the case of the de-facto complainant here that the signatures of the trustees were forged.
On the same breadth the de-facto complainant contended that the power of attorney holders or the Manager and workers of the trust property obtained signatures of the erstwhile trustees on the deed.
If the signature on certain document is not disputed, the case of forgery prima facie becomes questionable.

In view of such circumstances, this Court is of the view that the instant revision is required to be heard and accordingly, the same is admitted.
Since service is effected, and affidavit of service has been filed, the instant application be listed for final hearing under the heading "Contested Application" in the Monthly List of March, 2023.
In the meantime, the Investigating Officer is permitted to continue with the investigation,
examination of the accused persons by issuing notice under Section 41A of the Code of Criminal Procedure but will not take coercive step for a period of five weeks.
( Bibek Chaudhuri, J. )
